pending_items.title: In boost for Netanyahu, judges question corruption trial charges
pending_items.content:
Judges in the long-running corruption trial of Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu handed his defence a major boost on Wednesday in recommending the prosecution drop one of the cases in which he is accused of bribery.

The recommendations, which came as Israel's longest-serving prime minister fights for his political survival, were immediately cheered by Netanyahu's right-wing allies who demanded the trial be brought to an end.

Netanyahu's main rival Gadi Eisenkot has been tasked with forming a government after inconclusive October 27 elections and if Netanyahu is no longer prime minister, he would lose his leverage to avoid a potential jail sentence.

During a hearing in Jerusalem regarding three corruption cases against Netanyahu, judges recommended dropping one, reconsidering another and suggested resolving the third through an agreement, Israeli media reported.

In Case 4000, in which Netanyahu is accused of bribery, fraud and breach of trust, judges indicated there was little chance of a conviction.

That case is considered to be the most serious Netanyahu faces and concerns him allegedly offering regulatory favours for a telecoms company in exchange for favourable media coverage.

Netanyahu is alleged to have negotiated with Shaul Elovitch, the controlling shareholder of Israeli telecommunications giant Bezeq, to get positive coverage on his Walla news site in exchange for policies benefiting Bezeq.

On Wednesday, Israeli media reported Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman as saying that proving the bribery charge in that case faced "considerable difficulties".

Netanyahu, who has been in power on and off for three decades, has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing and denounced the cases as a politically motivated plot against him.

He is the first sitting Israeli premier to stand trial.

Israel's Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara, who was unusually summoned to the hearing on Wednesday, said she would consider the judges' recommendations and was ready for either a verdict or a plea deal.

In the second case, known as Case 2000, Netanyahu is accused of fraud and breach of trust over allegedly negotiating with the owner of the Yediot Aharonot newspaper for favourable media coverage.

In exchange, Netanyahu allegedly raised the possibility of pushing for legislation to limit the circulation of Israel Hayom, a free newspaper that is the main rival to Yediot.

Judges on Wednesday questioned whether his actions amounted to criminal conduct and recommended reconsidering the arguments in the case.

In a third case, Case 1000, Netanyahu faces fraud and breach of trust charges over allegedly receiving luxury gifts including cigars, champagne and jewellery from wealthy individuals in exchange for financial or personal favours.

Judges on Wednesday recommended finding an agreement in that case so it can be brought to a conclusion.

Netanyahu's allies welcomed the court's recommendations.

"After years of persecution against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the time has come to put an end to a trial that was flawed from the outset, that divides Israeli society and is exacting a heavy price from the state," Israel Katz, who is the defence minister in Netanyahu's caretaker government, wrote on X.

Far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said the cases against Netanyahu were "collapsing".

"This is a witch hunt by the deep state, which wants to bring down the right and its leader. We won't let them," he wrote on X.

Netanyahu's corruption trial opened in May 2020.

During his most recent term, which started in late 2022, Netanyahu proposed far-reaching judicial reforms that critics say sought to weaken the courts.

With coalition negotiations underway, Eisenkot's camp is already trying to start unravelling some of the Netanyahu-era judicial reforms in parliament.

US President Donald Trump had pushed Israeli President Isaac Herzog to issue Netanyahu a pardon, with Netanyahu himself submitting a formal request at the end of last year.
